safety_tips.tip: Wear footwear with good grip at Tsomgo Lake as some areas are slippery

safety_tips.tip: Be cautious on mountain roads and do not distract the driver
Avoid travelling late at night in isolated areas
Avoid night driving on mountain roads
Stick to planned routes and avoid isolated detours on mountain roads
Keep valuables and important documents safely stored and carry minimal cash
Avoid walking in poorly lit or deserted areas late at night
Wear seatbelts where available on steep, winding mountain roads
Walk slowly and avoid sudden exertion at Tsongmo Lake and Nathula Pass due to lower oxygen levels
Avoid alcohol and smoking at high altitude
Inform the driver immediately if headache, dizziness or nausea occurs at altitude
Follow driver and army instructions at all times on the Nathula route

Carry sunscreen and lip balm, especially at high altitude
Stay warm as weather changes quickly
Carry doctor-advised altitude medication such as Diamox, only if prescribed
Walk slowly and avoid exertion at high altitude
Avoid tea or coffee immediately at high altitude
Rest on the first day to adjust to altitude
Stay hydrated, especially on long drives and at higher altitudes
Prefer freshly cooked hot meals, especially in remote or high-altitude areas
Carry basic medicines for headache, motion sickness, cold and digestion
Use sunscreen (SPF 30–50) due to strong sun exposure at higher altitudes
Carry mosquito repellent for lower altitude areas
